newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU efforts boost bankruptcies - Dun & Bradstreet.
newsitem.headline: EMU efforts boost bankruptcies - Dun & Bradstreet.

text.p: Europe's efforts to achieve a common currency by 1999 are boosting corporate insolvencies as governments brake spending, business information agency Dun & Bradstreet Schimmelpfeng said on Thursday.
Bankruptcies in the 15 member states of the European Union should rise five percent to 200,000 this year, the report said.
Germany, Europe's largest economy, will be one of the hardest hit by the trend, it said. Insolvencies here are expected to rise 17 percent to 26,100 in 1996.
In east Germany, the rise is seen at 40 percent, as the construction industry in particular suffers from the economy's sluggishness.

France will continue to have a large number of business failures as the definition is stricter than in other countries, but the rise from last year will be less dramatic. Bankruptcies there should rise 3.8 percent to 58,100.
Britain will see about 40,900 bankruptcies, up one percent.
The Federal Statistics Office said on Thursday that German business insolvencies totalled 2,087 in June, and 12,499 in the first six months of the year.
